<reflection>
Low catalyst experiment didn't dramatically separate M5, M4, M3 from each other - they remain the top 3 with nearly identical NLL (~-60). M16, M11, M14, M20 still compete. Simple MM variants (M1, M2, M10, M15) and M12, M13 cluster around -40. The aim of discriminating top mechanisms was only partially achieved - second-order in cat didn't cleanly separate them, likely because fitting parameters adjusted to compensate.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
Key differences among leading mechanisms:
- M5: Productive pathway needs 2 cat molecules (catS+cat → catP+cat)
- M4: Different species X is required; if X is not supplied, behavior depends on initial conditions
- M3: Dimer cat2 is active; strong [cat]² dependence, saturation effects
- M11/M16: Substrate-dependent catalyst deactivation — HIGH substrate should accelerate deactivation
- M14/M20: CatS deactivation — also substrate-dependent indirectly
- M12/M17: Product-dependent deactivation — adding product should cause deactivation

The most diagnostic test: Add initial product. This directly probes product inhibition (M12, M17) vs. substrate-based inhibition (M11, M16) vs. substrate-independent (M5, M4, M3). With substantial initial product:
- M12/M17 show slower rates even from start
- M11/M16 rates depend only on remaining substrate
- M5 has catP intermediate so initial P could shift equilibrium
- Reverse reactions (k-2) become evident

High product (0.3 M) with moderate substrate (1.0 M) and moderate catalyst (0.01 M):
</hypothesis>
